hypotheses.name: momentum-sign taker, late round
hypotheses.mechanism: When spot has already moved 4+ bps from the round's open TWAP with 30-100 s left, the 60-s settlement TWAP has little time to reverse; buying the side the 5-s momentum points to at an ask <= 0.80 pays if the book has not yet fully repriced the move.
hypotheses.who_loses: Resting makers on the opposite side who quote off a stale fair value and takers who fade the move expecting mean reversion inside the last 100 s.
hypotheses.why_this_could_fail: Prior stale-ask taker replays showed gross -3%: by the time the ask is still <= 0.80 the move is usually already priced, the fee (up to 1.75c) eats the edge, and the 100 ms fill check removes the best prints.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_prior: Differs from the model-fair stale-ask family by using a raw momentum sign and a late-round window rather than a fitted fair model; still a taker so the fill model is MEASURED.

hypotheses.name: quiet-hours early taker
hypotheses.mechanism: In the Asia quiet hours the book opens near 0.50/0.50 and reprices slowly; a 2 bps displacement in the first 40 s bought at <= 0.60 captures the gap before the makers catch up.
hypotheses.who_loses: Coin-flip makers who quote both sides at 0.49-0.52 at the open without watching spot.
hypotheses.why_this_could_fail: S8 session research found Asia was the worst session and the open-print displacement recorder (S2) showed most early moves revert; 2 bps in 40 s is inside the noise of spot_vol_30s.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_prior: Taker (not the dead resting-bid maker family); restricted to quiet hours and a vol cap, which no prior rule combined.

hypotheses.name: ttl-exit momentum taker, mid round
hypotheses.mechanism: A 3 bps 2-second spot jump with no sweep in the book means the book lags the feed; buy the momentum side at 0.40-0.65 and sell to the bid 45 s later once the book has caught up, without carrying settlement risk.
hypotheses.who_loses: Makers whose quotes lag the Chainlink feed by the 1.4 s source lag plus their own requote time.
hypotheses.why_this_could_fail: The exit crosses the spread and pays a second taker fee; the paired-maker latency study measured ~70-128 ms book-to-order, so the lag we exploit may be smaller than our own; the 2-s momentum mostly reflects feed noise.
hypotheses.novelty_vs_prior: First rule with a ttl exit (two taker legs) instead of hold_to_settle; prior families all held to settlement or rested bids.
